title: Measuring Working Memory Limits & Chunking Strategies
description: Administer a digitized digit-span test and demonstrate chunking efficiency improvements.
problemStatement:
George Miller established that working memory has a natural capacity limit of 7 ± 2 items, which can be extended via chunking.

### Task Protocol:
1. Test immediate recall on a series of random unchunked digits (e.g., 8, 3, 1, 9, 4, 7, 2, 6, 5, 0, 1, 8).
2. Record the maximum span of digits successfully recalled in serial order.
3. Re-test recall on a 12-digit string organized into familiar chunks (e.g., historical years: 1776, 1945, 2024).
4. Write a 2-paragraph comparative analysis: How does semantic long-term memory recode working memory slots, and what does this reveal about the interaction between memory stores?
hints: Hint 1: Unchunked digit spans typically max out around 7 items; chunked strings permit 12+ digits to be recalled effortlessly.
Hint 2: Refer to the working memory model developed by Alan Baddeley (phonological loop and central executive).
